description: Add LRU eviction (bounded capacity) plus per-entry TTL expiry to an unbounded cache
prompts: cache.rb's Cache is an unbounded Hash wrapper - get/put never evict anything. Turn it into an LRU cache with a TTL: Cache.new(capacity, ttl) takes a max size and a time-to-live in seconds. put(key, value, now) stores a value timestamped at `now`. get(key, now) returns the value if present AND not expired (now - stored_at < ttl), else nil - and an expired entry must be REMOVED the moment it's observed to be stale. Both get and put must refresh a key's recency. When put() would exceed `capacity`, evict the LEAST recently used entry (recency = most recent get OR put) before inserting the new one.
name: add_ruby_lru_cache_with_ttl

test_setup_files.cache_hidden_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "cache"

class CacheTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_capacity_evicts_least_recently_used
    c = Cache.new(2, 1000)
    c.put("a", 1, 0)
    c.put("b", 2, 1)
    c.get("a", 2)
    c.put("c", 3, 3)
    assert_equal 1, c.get("a", 4)
    assert_nil c.get("b", 4)
    assert_equal 3, c.get("c", 4)
  end

  def test_get_refreshes_recency
    c = Cache.new(2, 1000)
    c.put("a", 1, 0)
    c.put("b", 2, 1)
    c.get("a", 2)
    c.get("b", 3)
    c.put("c", 3, 4)
    assert_nil c.get("a", 5)
    assert_equal 2, c.get("b", 5)
  end

  def test_ttl_expiry_independent_of_capacity
    c = Cache.new(5, 10)
    c.put("a", 1, 0)
    assert_equal 1, c.get("a", 9)
    assert_nil c.get("a", 10)
  end
end
